data.description:

Skillsoft Insider Transactions Over The Last Year

Notably, that recent purchase by Independent Director James Frankola was not the only time they bought Skillsoft shares this year. Earlier in the year, they paid US$6.06 per share in a US$303k purchase. That implies that an insider found the current price of US$6.19 per share to be enticing. That means they have been optimistic about the company in the past, though they may have changed their mind. While we always like to see insider buying, it's less meaningful if the purchases were made at much lower prices, as the opportunity they saw may have passed. Insiders own 13% of Skillsoft shares, worth about US$7.6m, according to our data. We do generally prefer see higher levels of insider ownership.

data.title: Dynex Capital (DX) Could Be 45% Undervalued As Dividend Terms Reset The Debate
data.description:

Recent price action has been weak, with Dynex Capital’s share price falling 8.63% over the past month and 13.49% year to date to US$12.18, even though the 1 year total shareholder return of 15.83% and 3 year total shareholder return of 50.36% indicate much stronger longer term momentum.

Price-to-Earnings of 7.1x: Is it justified?

On basic valuation math, Dynex Capital screens as inexpensive. The stock trades on a P/E of 7.1x at a last close of $12.18, which sits below both the broader US market and the Mortgage REIT peer group that cluster around higher earnings multiples.

P/E compares the current share price with the earnings per share and for mortgage REITs it often reflects how the market weighs income streams against balance sheet and funding risk. A lower ratio can signal that investors are demanding a wider margin of safety for those earnings or that they view current profitability as hard to repeat.

Dynex Capital complicates that simple read. The business shows very large earnings growth over the past year and high net profit margins of 84.7%, and its earnings are forecast to grow around 20% per year, faster than the wider US market. Yet the dividend yield of 16.75% is flagged as not being well covered by free cash flow, debt coverage by operating cash flow is weak, and all liabilities come from higher risk external borrowing. This can justify some caution from income focused investors even when reported earnings look strong.

Compared with the US Mortgage REITs industry average P/E of 8.4x, Dynex Capital trades at a clear discount. Against an estimated fair P/E of 13x, the current 7.1x multiple looks even more conservative. This implies the market is pricing the stock well below a level its earnings profile could potentially support if sentiment or risk perception shifted toward that fair ratio.

data.description:

data.title: Should Hirata India Partnership Require Action From ATS (TSX:ATS) Investors?
data.description:

To own ATS, you need to be comfortable with an automation specialist that leans heavily on complex projects, a growing services layer and acquisitions, while carrying meaningful debt and uneven near term order trends. The Hirata partnership in India plugs ATS equipment into an emerging semiconductor ecosystem, but it does not change the main near term swing factor, which is order momentum across core segments.

The bigger immediate risk still sits around elevated leverage, weaker transportation bookings and reliance on large, sometimes lumpy projects in areas like GLP 1 auto injectors. The India move slightly broadens optionality in electronics and semiconductor exposure, yet on its own it does not materially alter the balance between growth opportunities and balance sheet pressure.

With no other fresh announcements tied directly to semiconductors, the Hirata agreement itself is the key event to focus on here. It links ATS to backend automation demand in India, which fits the broader thesis that customers facing labor constraints and complex manufacturing requirements turn to higher value automation systems and lifecycle services.

For catalysts, investors are likely to watch whether this relationship helps ATS win more recurring work around servicing, upgrades and digital tools for installed equipment, not just one off projects.
